title: Two Ways to Build a World
genre: political philosophy and social science essay
centralQuestion: What remains of the partnership-domination idea when we refuse to romanticize the past?
thesis: Domination and partnership are recurrent coordination equilibria; technology and institutions change their relative cost without abolishing either repertoire.
audienceFit: readers interested in power, cooperation, institutional design, and how AI may reshape who can coordinate whom
motif: A stepped rust pyramid stands beside a teal lattice of linked nodes, two buildable architectures of coordination taken from the book's cover.

scenes.title: After the golden age
lines: A nearly forty-year-old idea claims societies keep organizing around partnership or domination.
Two Ways to Build a World keeps Riane Eisler's contrast and drops the peaceful golden age.
It treats domination and partnership as two recurring ways people coordinate under power.
Its central claim is that technology and institutions change which way is cheaper.

emotionalPlan.arc: recognition of an old contested idea, then clarity about what the book rescues and why it matters now
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book, its honest correction of the myth, and its central claim within twenty-five seconds.
voiceDirections: Open with quiet weight, let 'partnership or domination' land as the stakes.
Plain and fair, a small turn on 'drops'.
Lean in slightly on 'technology and institutions' and 'cheaper'.

scenes.title: From boxes to coordinates
lines: Instead of labelling whole civilizations, the book measures relationships along distinct dimensions.
It asks who can leave, speak, appeal, observe decisions, and impose sanctions.
Domination appears when wealth, media, office, and force convert into each other until escape disappears.
Hierarchy can stay legitimate when its purpose, scope, duration, review, and exit are clear.

emotionalPlan.arc: analytical build from method to the warning about closing loops, released by a constructive distinction
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's method: a coordinate system of concrete questions, the danger of convertible status, and hierarchy without domination.
voiceDirections: Measured and clear, as if laying out a map.
Brisk list, a short beat between each verb.
Warmer and calm, release the tension.

scenes.title: Partnership needs teeth
lines: Drawing on commons governance, it shows cooperation needs boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, and appeal.
Artificial intelligence can become an empire machine, or it can lower the cost of partnership.
Start with Chapter 3, From Binary to Coordinate System, and learn to map who holds power.

emotionalPlan.arc: practical firmness, a sharp present-day stake, then an inviting concrete starting point
emotionalPlan.purpose: Deliver the book's design lessons and its AI stakes, and give the reader a specific place to begin.
voiceDirections: Contrast the two halves, slight pause before 'or'.
Friendly and direct, name the chapter clearly, warm lift on 'who holds power'.
